components.cost_effect: Two oracle calls plus two dot products per trial.

components.key_estimate: Symmetric inputs pass surely; nonsymmetric inputs are detected with probability at least 1/4 per trial, as used by the source.

variants.cost: At most 2r exact right-matvec calls. Separately, each trial samples 2n Gaussian coordinates, computes two length-n dot products and makes one scalar comparison. These require O(n) local arithmetic and O(n) working storage when trials are streamed. This operation count is bookkeeping for the displayed implementation, not a runtime theorem from the source. Exact real sampling/arithmetic is idealized; bit complexity and internal oracle work are not bounded.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Section 3.3, Theorem 4 proof, PDF p17; explicit schedule at thm.P086.symmetry /content/proofs/0/full_local_argument
variants.name: Real Gaussian bilinear tester
variants.output: One binary label: symmetric or nonsymmetric. No matrix reconstruction or numerical distance estimate.
public_inputs: Exact right-matvec oracle for a fixed real square matrix
variants.query_and_update: Query y=Mu and z=Mv. Compute a=sum_i u_i z_i and b=sum_i v_i y_i. If a!=b, return nonsymmetric immediately. Otherwise advance to the next trial.
variants.requirements: Exact arithmetic, exact comparison and ideal Gaussian sampling. Access to M is only through right products; a transpose oracle is unnecessary.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set r=ceil(log(1/delta)/log(4/3)); initialize the pass flag to true. For each trial sample two fresh independent vectors u,v with independent N(0,1) coordinates; all trials are independent.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run at most r trials; return symmetric if every equality holds. The source supplies independent repetition and the >=1/4 detection bound; the integer r is a local explicit schedule proved in the linked Theorem. All vectors may be sampled before any queries, so early stopping does not require adaptive query choices.

use_restrictions: Exact real-arithmetic query model only; local arithmetic and sampling are charged separately from oracle queries.
